strategy_title: Autotune Block Size to Increase Wave Count and Occupancy
strategy_description: When a Triton kernel shows fewer than 1.0 waves/SM (SOLBottleneck), low achieved occupancy (<60%), and high 'No Eligible' warp percentage (>60%), the block size is likely too small to saturate the GPU. Adding @triton.autotune with configs spanning a wide range of XBLOCK/YBLOCK values (e.g., 64–1024) and num_warps (4–16) allows the runtime to select the configuration that maximizes wave count and hides memory latency. In this case, doubling the block size from 128 to 256 (selected by autotuner) doubled waves/SM from 0.74 to 1.48, raised achieved occupancy from 54.7% to 68.3%, and cut warp cycles per issued instruction from 30.3 to 17.4, yielding a 1.45x speedup.
slow_pseudocode:
@triton.jit
def kernel(in_ptr, out_ptr, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK: tl.constexpr, XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    # fixed tile sizes, hardcoded at launch
    ...

# launch with fixed config
grid = (cdiv(xnumel, 128), cdiv(ynumel, 8))
kernel[grid](in_ptr, out_ptr, ynumel, xnumel, YBLOCK=8, XBLOCK=128)
applicable_when: Triton kernel has waves/SM < 1.0 (SOLBottleneck rule triggered), achieved occupancy < 60%, 'No Eligible' warp % > 60%, and issue slots busy < 35%. The kernel uses 2D tiling (XBLOCK x YBLOCK) with fixed hardcoded launch parameters. Problem size is large enough that larger block sizes won't over-partition the grid.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel already has waves/SM > 2.0 or achieved occupancy > 80%. Kernel body has register pressure that would be worsened by larger blocks. Grid is already large relative to SM count. Autotuning overhead is unacceptable (e.g., very short-lived kernels called once).
framework_notes: Triton-specific: @triton.autotune must be placed immediately before @triton.jit. The grid lambda must use meta['XBLOCK'] and meta['YBLOCK'] instead of hardcoded values. XBLOCK/YBLOCK must NOT be passed explicitly at launch when autotuning — the autotuner injects them. num_stages in triton.Config controls software pipelining depth. Equivalent in CUDA: use __launch_bounds__ or grid-stride loops with different block sizes benchmarked via occupancy calculator.
